deliverables: Intersect budget administration, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, administered by Intersect for the Mithril Protocol project.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continuous development through Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: Mithril uses stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way so nodes and applications can verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
The proposal states that current full node synchronisation is slow and light clients rely on centralized trust.

Funding Mithril's continued development through Intersect is claimed to help Cardano scale while preserving decentralization guarantees and reducing dependency on centralized indexers and hosted APIs.
The proposal claims full alignment with the Infrastructure & Research Excellence and Adoption & Utility strategic pillars, and partial alignment with Community & Ecosystem Growth.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposal states the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
The budget allocates 3,699,440 ada to Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada to the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
The proposal states audit and oversight costs are included in overhead, with independent oversight by Intersect and technically capable third parties plus milestone-based disbursement controls.

The proposal states Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs but has worked on Mithril for several years through IOG-funded collaboration.
Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multi-party authorization rules, and a dashboard for community auditability.

summary: The document requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration, presents strategic and technical rationale, cites Intersect budget-process approval and NCL compliance, and describes smart-contract-based custody and oversight, but it does not include a complete budget breakdown, feasibility assessment, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, or failure-mode analysis.
